text: NUMERICAL METHODS ATLAS · INTRODUCTION & SHARING Numerical methods. Evidence you can follow. From assumptions and original papers to public code, fixed inputs and result checks. A resource for graduate students, researchers and the AI assistants supporting their work. Sources and assumptions Read the applicability, approximations, units and boundaries. Fixed inputs and public code Retain the edition and input, then run a representative example. References and result checks Distinguish analytic and numerical references, conservation and residuals. 165Methods & components 255Research publications 95Equations & models 174Test problems 165 counts existing methods and building blocks. The method map has 171 records: 155 educational/related-code, 10 reading-only and 6 planned. These are not counts of complete production solvers. The 22 runnable examples are a subset of the 174 problems, not an addition. Find a starting point Choose from 22 fixed-input examples Each entry provides conditions, edition, input, commands, JSON/CSV and numerical tolerances. Barnes–Hut: 192 particles against direct summationCompare tree and direct forces for 192 particles; inspect force error, the fully opened limit and interaction counts. Hydrogenic atoms: analytic references and grid refinementCompare energy, radial wavefunctions and grid refinement with analytic references for the specified Z=1,2 bound states. Helium: closed-shell HF and exchange-only LDASolve spherical 1s² helium with RHF and exchange-only LDA; compare SCF convergence, energies and electron count with independent finite-basis references. Periodic sine advection: upwind and analytic transportCompare periodic sine transport with analytic translation; check refinement, mean conservation and the maximum principle. Sod shock tube: Godunov-type update and self-similar referenceCompare the Sod shock tube with a self-similar Riemann solution; check decreasing density error, positivity and boundary-flux balances. Shu–Osher: characteristic WENO-Z and a numerical referenceCompute shock–density-wave interaction and compare 100/200-point solutions with an 800-point same-method numerical reference. 1D Poisson: Dirichlet sine solution and second-order refinementCompare the Thomas solution with sin(πx), separating continuous error, a recomputed discrete residual and second-order grid refinement. 2D Poisson: CG, multigrid and P1 FEMInspect CG/multigrid on the same discrete system and P1 FEM, comparing FD maximum error with separate FEM L2/H1-seminorm refinement. 1D Bratu: Newton–GMRES on the lower branchCompute the lower branch with Newton–GMRES and check its analytic solution, recomputed nonlinear residual and second-order refinement. Harmonic oscillator: Verlet phase error and energyCompare Verlet trajectories with analytic oscillation; inspect state error, original-energy deviation and time reversal. Stiff cosine-tracking ODE: SDIRK2Compare stiff cosine tracking with its analytic solution under step refinement, plus a separate strongly damped problem. Smooth function: Legendre projection and GLL interpolationCompare Legendre projection and GLL interpolation of exp(x); use higher-order reference quadrature for p-refinement, coefficients and orthogonality. Periodic PM particles: mass, internal force and mesh fieldInspect CIC mass, self-force, net internal force and wrapping for 19 fixed particles; separately check mesh potential/acceleration for a sinusoidal density. Periodic Taylor–Green vortex: velocity, decay and divergenceCompare periodic-vortex velocity and viscous energy decay with analytic references; inspect discrete divergence, pressure gauge and space/time sensitivity. Brio–Wu: HLLD and a conservatively restricted numerical referenceCompare 64/128-cell HLLD solutions with a 512-cell numerical reference; inspect density, pressure, constant longitudinal field, balances and fallbacks. Logistic growth: analytic solution and time refinementOne dimensionless population. Compare RK4 with the analytic solution at every output time; check nonnegativity and time refinement. Excludes reaction–diffusion and multispecies models. SIR: independent DOP853 reference, conservation and convergenceClosed homogeneous population-fraction SIR. Compare RK4 with independently implemented SciPy DOP853; check conservation, nonnegativity and time convergence. Excludes SEIR, spatial spread and calibration to observations. Monte Carlo: integral errors and interval coverage across 256 seedsIntegrate x² under U[0,1]. Compare 256 independent seeds with analytic integral and variance, checking N^-1/2 RMS scaling and interval coverage. Excludes MCMC and rare events. Itô SDE: strong convergence with coupled Brownian pathsEuler–Maruyama for scalar geometric Brownian motion. Coarse/fine steps and analytic endpoints share the same Brownian paths; measure strong RMS error across 4096 paths. Does not validate general SDEs, MCMC or weak convergence order. H₂ molecular RHF: independent reference, SCF and s-basis refinementIsolated Born–Oppenheimer nonrelativistic two-electron closed-shell H₂. Compare STO-3G and nested s-Gaussian spaces at three separations. Numerical RHF validation, not molecular DFT, periodic, complete-basis or correct-dissociation validation. Periodic-He KS-LDA: Gamma, k meshes, basis and SCFFixed one-atom simple-cubic He cell (lattice constant 4 bohr, two valence electrons, unpolarized LDA_X plus VWN5, local GTH). A PySCF execution/validation workflow. Eleven settings separately compare k sampling, Gaussian orbital basis, auxiliary FFT grid and SCF; Gamma and 2³ are compared with independent DFTK plane waves. Equilibrium helium, complete-basis, metals and general materials remain unvalidated. Periodic-He₂ forces: analytic derivatives, finite differences and BOMD interfaceAsymmetric two-He periodic cell with local GTH and LDA exchange plus VWN5. Compare PySCF analytic forces, including Gaussian-basis derivatives, with energy finite differences for all six coordinates and independent DFTK plane waves. Separate force basis, k-point, SCF and FFT refinement. BOMD coverage is a force interface and short step comparison; long NVE, CPMD and general materials remain unvalidated.
